newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower, BIS slides to Vendex bid.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower, BIS slides to Vendex bid.

text.p: French shares opened lower on weaker bond prices on Tuesday and caution ahead of important U.S. statistics due out on Thursday and Friday, brokers said.
Temporary work agency BIS, suspended since December 30, reopened nearly seven percent down at 496 francs to trade near the 490 franc per share bid price of Dutch Vendex International.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 11.32 points or 0.49 percent at 2,295.35 at 0911 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,300 from 2,313 on Monday's close.
The CAC found support at 2,294.01 in early exchanges.

Today's U.S. factory goods orders, due at 1500 GMT, are on average forecast to show a 0.6 percent fall after a 0.9 percent rise in October. "Factory goods are not that important, the PPI is," a dealer said.
December U.S. producer prices, due Thursday at 1330 GMT, are seen up 0.3 percent for the month. Thursday will also see U.S. jobless claims, expected to be up 353,000.
Friday's non-farm payrolls are seen up by 192,000.
AXA added another 0.12 percent to 333.90 francs on capital gain on Lafayette stake sale and NatMut outlook.
Thomson-CSF gained 2.3 percent to 173.10 francs on anewspaper report the French government is planning to sell its 60 percent stake through a private auction among "qualified bidders".
Lagardere, down 0.21 percent at 141.50, and Alcatel Alsthom, down 0.24 percent at 415 francs, are expected to be among the Thomson-CSF bidders.
AGF, up 0.18 percent to 168 francs, sold its Banque de Phenix unit to ABN Amro Holding for an as yet undisclosed consideration.
